nodes.label: General conventions (ABC roles, dataclasses, int cents)
nodes.rationale: Shared conventions across templates: ABC roles, dataclass data, dependencies injected through the constructor, creation in one place, int cents, specific errors, no id or type names.

nodes.label: Abstract Factory
nodes.rationale: Use when product families must be used together. Precaution: adding a product type forces changes to AbsFactory and every factory.

nodes.label: Builder
nodes.rationale: Use when an object is assembled in ordered steps with several configurations. Precaution: with only optional fields and no order, a dataclass with keyword arguments is enough.

nodes.label: Factory Method
nodes.rationale: Move instantiation out of the client, with a registry (Simple Factory) or subclass-decided factory method. Precaution: with two products that will not grow, an if is clearer.

nodes.label: Prototype
nodes.rationale: Clone a configured object for variations. Precaution: copy.copy shares mutable parts while deepcopy copies everything, including what should be shared.

nodes.label: Singleton
nodes.rationale: Use only when exactly one instance must exist and many unrelated modules need it. Precaution: a singleton is global state in disguise that hides dependencies and leaks state between tests; prefer injecting it from the composition root.

nodes.label: Adapter
nodes.rationale: Wrap an existing class whose interface does not match, without modifying either side. Precaution: prefer the object adapter (composition) over the class adapter (multiple inheritance).

nodes.label: Bridge
nodes.rationale: Split a hierarchy that grows along two independent dimensions and connect them by reference. Precaution: with only one real dimension the bridge is indirection without benefit.

nodes.label: Composite
nodes.rationale: Let leaves and groups share one interface and let groups delegate to children. Precaution: do not push leaf-only operations such as birthdate into the shared interface.

nodes.label: Decorator
nodes.rationale: Add responsibilities to a concrete object at runtime by wrapping it with the same interface. Precaution: rules the hierarchy used to enforce must be validated in the decorator constructor, and isinstance no longer recognises the wrapped object.

nodes.label: Facade
nodes.rationale: Give clients one method per use case over a subsystem. Precaution: a facade simplifies access without forbidding it, and absorbing foreign responsibilities turns it into a god class.

nodes.label: Flyweight
nodes.rationale: Share the immutable part of very many objects from a cached factory. Precaution: the flyweight must be immutable and the saving must be measured before and after.

nodes.label: Proxy
nodes.rationale: Control access to an object (permissions, lazy loading, caching) with a stand-in that has the same interface. Precaution: the proxy must follow the real interface and clients must receive the proxy.

nodes.label: Observer
nodes.rationale: Let unknown dependents subscribe to changes. Precaution: detach observers that are no longer used (lapsed listener), since one slow or failing observer affects the rest.

nodes.label: State
nodes.rationale: When every method branches on the same state code, give each state its own class and let the context delegate. Precaution: with two trivial states an if is clearer.

nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.rationale: Encapsulate interchangeable algorithms and pass one to the context at runtime. Precaution: if strategies hold no state, passing a Callable is enough in Python.

nodes.label: Template Method
nodes.rationale: Write a shared sequence of steps once in a base class and let subclasses fill the steps. Precaution: the skeleton is fixed by inheritance; if the whole algorithm varies, use Strategy.
